source_text.Q-1040: LOW, test-only, CI/test lane. test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs polling loops at ~L518 and ~L817 (Enum.reduce_while(1..20) with Process.sleep(10) = ~200 ms of observation) wait for a supervised Lua child while the script/call runs only timeout_ms 300; under host load the child can finish or not yet have started inside that window, so the assertion that a real in-flight child was observed can miss it. Fix: make the script deterministic instead of time-bound (script blocks on a message from the test, or the poll waits on a :started message plus a monotonic deadline well above the script's life; the script's duration is controlled by the test, not a sleep) so the window cannot close before the test looks; no global timing change. Mutation proof: a mutant that never spawns the child must still fail; stress: 100 consecutive runs under max_cases concurrency green (quote command and result). Acceptance: (1) both observation windows no longer depend on a fixed ~200 ms poll inside a 300 ms script; (2) mutant that never spawns the child still fails both tests; (3) 100 consecutive local runs under concurrency green, command and result quoted. Overlap: no open queue issue on executor_test; ISS-0456 (wasm_hang) is a different file. GH #2379.

result.summary: ISS-1040 test change validated independently. Both observation windows replaced by await_own_child/2 (own-child match via $callers, 5000 ms monotonic deadline, 5 ms retry) with timeout_ms 30_000 and test-controlled release by Process.exit(child,:kill); no fixed ~200 ms poll inside a 300 ms script remains. No findings.
